_comment: The EMPIRE / Williams 20-Year Plan MSP buy box, encoded so the scanner can score strategic fit — not just market valuation. Deal 1 is a Dallas-based platform acquisition (H2 2031) financed SBA 7(a) + seller note (~$700K equity in), operated on an AI-native model with a legal-vertical edge, bought at ~3-4.5x and re-rated to 8-12x at exit. Tuck-ins follow at 2.5-3.5x SDE. Edit these to change how deals are ranked.

platformWindow.comment: Earnings on either basis. Above ~$1.8M EBITDA the ~$6M price bumps the $5M SBA 7(a) cap and forces disproportionate equity — the plan's explicit price-discipline line.

requirements.gmInPlace: non-negotiable — a GM/service manager who owns client relationships so the owner can exit

verticalTiebreaker.note: Generalist chassis with vertical concentration beats a vertical-only identity. Chassis quality outweighs vertical fit for Deal 1.

operatingThesis.aiMarginUplift: Agentic ticket triage, auto-documentation, and L1 auto-resolution move gross margin from the industry's 10-15% toward ~35%. Re-rate upside lives in contractual MRR you can protect while AI takes out L1 labor — NOT in book-of-hours or resale revenue.
operatingThesis.reRate: Buy at ~3x, re-rate to 8-12x EBITDA at a 2039-41 exit/recap.
operatingThesis.onshoreThesis: The plan's edge is a legal / professional-services vertical (confidentiality- and compliance-sensitive buyers) plus AI-driven L1 automation. Offshore labor arbitrage is the OLD margin lever that this plan's own AI thesis makes obsolete, it clashes with the trust/compliance expectations of the target vertical, and it depresses the exit multiple consolidators will pay. Onshore, relationship-run delivery is the fit; offshore earnings are lower quality and less transferable even when the multiple looks cheap.
